briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Momentum Building: MI Courts & Campaigns Turn on the Tax, DEA Clears Another Rescheduling Hurdle
briefs.top: In Michigan, both major gubernatorial campaigns are now on record against the 24% wholesale tax while the state Supreme Court hands operators a real enforcement win on vehicle searches. Nationally, DEA's rescheduling process cleared another procedural checkpoint and MSOs are back on the M&A trail, with psychedelics posting a parallel breakthrough as Compass Pathways' psilocybin program races toward a potential first-in-class FDA approval.

local.text: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James pledged to repeal or sharply roll back the 24% wholesale cannabis tax as part of his 'Freedom Agenda,' arguing it 'drives up prices, gives illegal operators a competitive edge, and has already fallen far short of revenue projections' — and the Michigan Cannabis Industry Association is now touting the pledge to build momentum for relief.

The Michigan Supreme Court ruled 5-2 that police can't conduct a warrantless vehicle search based on marijuana odor alone, a decision one House of Dank sales manager called 'really nice and relieving' for finally lifting stigma off legal consumers and, by extension, the retailers who serve them.

Despite tax headwinds, Michigan's market stayed the country's third-largest by monthly volume, with July 2026 sales hitting $260.6 million; over 30 million units moved at an average item price of just $8.65 — the lowest of any major U.S. market and a sign consumer demand remains sticky.

Industry trackers note July 2026 delivered back-to-back Supreme Court wins reshaping enforcement, even as two tax lawsuits and a widening gap between wholesale-tax projections and actual collections remain live — a sign the legal battlefield is shifting in operators' favor on multiple fronts at once.

Cannabis operators pressed their constitutional challenge to the wholesale tax, arguing the layered levy creates unlawful 'tax pyramiding' on consumers — a case MiCIA calls 'exceptionally strong,' keeping the door open for a court-ordered rollback that would ease margins across the supply chain.

national.text: DEA's cannabis rescheduling process cleared another critical procedural checkpoint in mid-August, keeping Schedule III movement on track — a shift that would eliminate 280E tax penalties and cut effective operator tax rates from roughly 60% to the mid-20s.

FDA granted Compass Pathways a rolling NDA review plus a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for COMP360, its psilocybin treatment for treatment-resistant depression — a designation that could shrink final review to just one to two months, putting the first-ever approved psilocybin drug within reach.

M&A is heating up fast: Vireo Growth closed a $49 million buy of PharmaCann's Colorado retail assets in early August and separately struck a deal to acquire Cannabist Company operations across five states, signaling renewed consolidation confidence across the MSO sector.

Capital access is loosening ahead of rescheduling — Cresco Labs secured a $50 million revolving credit facility from Needham Bank, with CEO Charlie Bachtell calling it a 'powerful, non-dilutive tool' to fund acquisitions and position for a future uplisting to a senior U.S. exchange.

Compass Pathways is now partnering with the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, donating its COMP360 psilocybin formulation for a multi-site VA study on treatment-resistant depression and PTSD in veterans — broadening institutional and government buy-in for psychedelic medicine.
